units.title: Live: the worst night of cuts so far
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 22:50. Here we go again. The co-op's fault map is showing interruptions on the Gilliver spur and the Lisle pier circuit, about 500 customers. Tonight is also the first night ferry crossing for a week, so we'll be keeping an eye on both. Updates here through the night.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:25. A second fault, this time on the Port Ammet north feeder. The streets behind the market and the hospital's outpatient block are dark; the hospital says its main buildings are on generators and patients are not affected. Around 1,300 customers are now off supply.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:45. Some good news: the night ferry left Port Ammet at 22:40 exactly and has arrived at Lisle under its new floodlights. A listener on the pier says the boat 'looked like a lit-up birthday cake coming across'. It's on its way to Gilliver now.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:30. The Brackwater feeder has tripped as well, taking out the village and the outskirts of Tollinby. That makes four separate circuits tonight. The co-op says it has every available crew out and has asked people not to call the fault line unless there's a dangerous situation such as a line down.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 01:25. Messages are coming in from all over. A Tollinby listener says her street came to its front doors when the lights went, 'like a fire drill with nobody in charge'. In Port Ammet, the taxi rank on the front is running on headlights. Stay in if you can, and check on anyone who lives alone.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 02:15. Port Ammet north is back. Brackwater and Tollinby are back. Gilliver and Lisle pier remain off, around 480 customers. The co-op has given no cause, but says crews are 'investigating the coastal circuits'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 03:20. Gilliver and Lisle are back on supply after more than four hours. That was the longest interruption of the month. Priority-register customers in Gilliver were phoned by the co-op during the night, we're told, and two were offered a place in the village hall, which has its own generator.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 04:00. That's it from the live desk tonight. Thank you to everyone who stayed with us and sent in messages; there were more than two hundred of them. We'll have the co-op's response in the morning bulletins. Get some sleep.

units.title: Bin rounds stalled as cuts lock depot gate
units.author: courier
units.text: Recycling collections in parts of Port Ammet have fallen behind for a third week after night-time power cuts repeatedly disabled the electric gate at the council's waste depot, trapping collection lorries inside until staff could open it by hand.

units.author: courier
units.text: The council said the gate's manual override required two members of staff and that early-morning crews had on several occasions been unable to leave on time. 'The lorries are fine; the fuel is fine; it's the gate,' a spokesperson said. A battery backup for the gate has been ordered.

units.author: courier
units.text: Residents of Rope Walk, where more than thirty bins have stood at the kerb since the start of the week, said they had been told collections would resume 'as soon as possible'. One retired resident told the Courier he had counted them twice and written to the council with the figure.

units.title: Co-op reminds staff not to discuss faults online
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power Co-op has reminded its field staff that they are not authorised to discuss network faults in public, after linemen were quoted on local forums disputing the company's explanation for this month's night-time power cuts.

units.author: courier
units.text: Forum posts attributed to co-op employees in recent days have said that several faults occurred on clear, dry nights and that patrols found nothing on the lines. A local amateur weather observer has published readings showing no fog on at least two of the nights in question.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op said the reminder was 'routine' and that it valued its crews' expertise. 'Our engineers are working extremely hard in difficult conditions,' a spokesperson said. 'Technical findings are reviewed centrally and shared when they are complete. Speculation doesn't help anyone.'

units.author: courier
units.text: The spokesperson said salt-fog corrosion remained the 'leading hypothesis' but that 'other contributing factors are being examined', the first time the co-op has suggested the cause may not be corrosion alone. It did not say what those factors were.

units.title: Dock pay talks resume after a week's pause
units.author: weypost
units.text: Pay talks between Weyhaven port's operators and the dockers' union resumed yesterday after a week's pause, with both sides describing the meeting as 'constructive' and agreeing to meet again before the end of the month.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The union is seeking a rise in line with the cost of living and changes to night-shift rotas, which members say have become harder to cover since the cold snap began. The operators have offered a smaller rise linked to new crane-handling targets.

units.author: weypost
units.text: No industrial action has been called. Shipping lines using the port said they had seen no disruption so far, though one haulier said container collections at night had slowed because 'nobody wants the late slot in this weather'.

units.title: Grieve stays quiet on Holm as contract nears its end
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve Land Services has again declined to comment on the progress of its clearance of Kittering Holm, which enters its final week shortly. The firm's 30-day contract is among the fastest island clearances attempted in the region.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Industry observers note that Grieve has a long record of remote work, including a northern clearance some years ago that the firm does not list among its references. Asked about this, a Grieve spokesperson said the company 'does not comment on historical contracts'.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Contract terms reported earlier in the journal, a rate per tree plus a day rate per worker, put the emphasis firmly on speed. 'The money is in the trees, but the costs are in the days,' one competing contractor said. 'The last week of a job like that is when people cut corners. I'd hope Grieve's people are being sensible.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The owner, Ardent Vale Holdings, has made no public statement on the island since a brief community note earlier in the month. It has not said whether it will replant, build or simply hold the land once the clearance is complete.

units.title: Letters: lamps, linemen and the island
units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, my grandmother kept a lamp in her window in Gilliver for sixty years and never once explained it. I have started doing the same in Port Ammet this month. I don't know why either, and I find I don't mind. It is a small, warm thing to do in a cold month. Name and address supplied.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, I note that Sound Power Co-op has told its linemen to stop talking to the public. Those linemen have been out in minus five every night this fortnight and have been more honest with us than anyone in an office. If the co-op wants trust, it should start by answering their questions. Retired engineer, Tollinby.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, I am tired of reading speculation about the people working on Kittering Holm. They are tree fellers on a contract, not characters in a story. If anyone wants to help them, they could ask the company to make sure they are properly supplied and properly paid, and leave the rest alone. Former forestry worker, Lisle.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, may I, through your pages, thank the night ferry crew for their return. I have watched the boat cross from my window on Lisle for forty years and the week without it was the quietest I can remember. Welcome back. Pier Road, Lisle.

units.title: Tenants ask for independent survey of Dellow Court
units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents of Dellow Court have asked Kerrow Estates to commission an independent survey of the building's stairwells and lift, saying a month of faults has left some tenants afraid to use the stairs even after the lighting was repaired.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association said it had collected more than forty signatures. 'We're not asking for anything dramatic,' its secretary said. 'Have someone who doesn't work for the landlord walk the building, check the doors and the ventilation and the acoustics, and write it down. Then people can stop guessing.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates said it would 'consider the request carefully' and pointed to its recent replacement of the stairwell timer relay. The lift, which has broken down repeatedly this month, will be out of service for planned maintenance on the next working day.

units.title: Gilliver boats short of ice as quay plant stays shut
units.author: courier
units.text: Gilliver's creel boats have been buying ice from Port Ammet since the ice plant on the village's north quay closed for maintenance last week, adding an hour's round trip to some skippers' mornings during the coldest spell of the year.

units.author: courier
units.text: The plant's operator said the shutdown, which includes replacing its circulation pump and isolating the whole site at the switchboard, was planned in the summer and had 'nothing to do with the power cuts'. It expects to reopen at the weekend.

units.author: courier
units.text: 'It's the irony that gets you,' said one fisherman. 'Minus five every morning and we're driving to town for ice.' The harbour chandlery said it had sold out of cool boxes twice.

units.author: met
units.text: Forecast for the Marrow Sound, today and tonight. A last calm, cold day under high pressure. Sunny, light winds. Maximum 1 °C. Tonight clear at first with frost, minimum −4 °C, cloud thickening from the west towards dawn. Tomorrow: the cold spell ends. Rain spreading from the west from around midday, heavy at times overnight, with winds freshening southerly. Outlook: unsettled and much milder, with rain for several days.

units.author: met
units.text: Frost warning, final night. Widespread hard frost tonight in sheltered areas; −4 °C to −6 °C inland. Ice on untreated roads and paths. As rain arrives tomorrow on frozen ground there is a risk of ice on surfaces for a short time before temperatures rise. Take care on the roads tomorrow morning.

units.author: met
units.text: Tides and small craft, Port Ammet reference. High water 04:51 (4.0 m) and 17:15 (4.2 m). Low water 11:04 and 23:30. Small-craft conditions good today. Small-craft warning likely from tomorrow afternoon as southerly winds increase ahead of the rain.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines service update. Night sailings resume tonight. The 22:40 Port Ammet - Lisle - Gilliver sailing and the return 00:15 Gilliver - Lisle - Port Ammet sailing will operate. Additional lighting is in use on the vessel and at the Gilliver and Lisle slips. Passengers are asked to remain on deck areas that are lit and to follow crew instructions when boarding.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines: the 22:40 sailing from Port Ammet departed on time and arrived at Gilliver at 23:52. The return sailing will leave Gilliver at 00:15 as scheduled. Shore power at the Gilliver slip is currently interrupted; slip lighting is operating from its generator.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: supply restored. Interruptions overnight affected Gilliver, Lisle pier and parts of Port Ammet between 23:20 and 03:14. All customers are now back on supply. Investigation into the causes of recent faults on the coastal network is continuing. Thank you for your patience.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: night advisory. Interruptions remain possible on the coastal and inland networks tonight. Additional crews are on standby. Please check the fault map before calling us, keep freezers closed, and make sure any medical equipment has backup power. Never approach a fallen line.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: unplanned interruptions. Gilliver spur and Lisle pier from 22:48; Port Ammet north feeder from 23:21. Approximately 1,300 customers affected. Crews dispatched to both locations. We will update this notice as soon as we can give restoration times.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: further interruption. Brackwater feeder from 00:27, affecting Brackwater village, the reservoir pumping station and the Tollinby outskirts. Approximately 900 additional customers. The pumping station has switched to standby generation.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: update. Port Ammet north restored 01:58. Brackwater and Tollinby restored 02:11. Gilliver and Lisle pier restored 03:16. All customers are now on supply. Customers whose interruption exceeded the standard period may be entitled to a payment; details on our website.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council: waste collections. Some collections in Port Ammet are delayed because power interruptions have affected access at the waste depot. Crews are working to catch up. Please leave bins out until collected. A backup power supply for the depot gate has been ordered.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council: Brackwater reservoir lane. Culvert works at the Brackwater junction will continue under temporary signals until the end of next week. In heavy rain the reservoir lane may flood near the culvert; if it does, it will be closed and a diversion signed via the Tollinby road.

units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. Skerry buoy, east of Gilliver: the light remains unlit. Servicing has been postponed until conditions allow following the forecast change in weather. Mariners navigating the channel between Gilliver and Kittering Holm at night should exercise particular caution.

units.title: Timesheet received KH-01
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Your timesheet for site KH-01, day 22, has been received and queued for processing. No exceptions were found. Period 3 closes at the end of day 24; any corrections must be submitted before close. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Provisional statement available: period 3
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: A provisional statement for site KH-01, period 3, is now available on the payroll portal. Figures are provisional until the period closes and the verified tree count is confirmed by Operations. Ref GLS-PS-0323-P. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Toasty hands, three for two!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Cold fingers? Not on our watch! This week only, our reusable hand warmers are three for two. Click, squeeze, and enjoy up to six hours of lovely heat. Perfect for early starts, late finishes, and those long nights when the generator's the only other thing awake! Plus: free delivery on orders over $40.

units.title: Correction to this week's newsletter
units.author: council_news
units.text: In this week's newsletter we described recent overnight interruptions as 'Sound Power works'. Sound Power Co-op has asked us to clarify that the interruptions are unplanned faults and not scheduled works. We apologise for any confusion. Updates are available on the co-op's fault map. The photo competition deadline is unchanged.

units.title: Client call
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the client call happened this morning. Short, as usual. They asked about the end date and nothing else. They're very hands-off; I don't think they'd notice if we sent them a photo of the moon. Thanks for getting the tally on the system. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Supply boat: rain from tomorrow
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the forecast turns tomorrow, rain from midday and wind getting up. The skipper would like to run the next drop early rather than late so he isn't coming alongside in the dark with a swell. Please make sure the landing's clear and someone's there to take the lines. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, one more thing on the boat: the Gilliver fuel berth was off again overnight in the power cut, so if the diesel isn't pumped in time he'll bring what he has and come back. Please don't run the generator any harder than you need to until he's been. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Your own saw
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, accounts noticed the saw on the site inventory is your own rather than company kit. That's absolutely fine. Just so you know, it isn't covered by our equipment insurance, so please keep it logged in the site book and look after it. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Vehicle on site
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the truck on the Holm is down as yours, not the company's, so I need to remind you it isn't covered by Grieve's fleet policy. Head office would like it to stay on the yard tracks and off anything that looks soft once the rain arrives. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: End of contract
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, head office has started on the end-of-contract plan: kit back, camp down, crew travel. I'll send it through once it's signed off, probably early next week. Nothing for you to do yet. If there's anything on site you think needs special handling, let me know. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Courier letters page
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the Courier letters page today had someone asking that the crew be left alone and properly supplied and paid. I thought you'd like to know that people are on your side. Head office didn't comment and I'd rather we didn't either. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Before period 3 closes
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, period 3 closes tomorrow night and payroll still show crew wages outstanding on KH-01. If it isn't settled by close, it goes to Operations as an arrears case, and that's a formal process I'd rather neither of us had to deal with. Please sort it tonight if you possibly can. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Not a question this time
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello. Not a question this time, I promise. During last night's power cut, two people rang the Courier to ask whether the crew on the Holm were all right. I told them truthfully that I didn't know and that the company hadn't said. I thought you'd want to know that people are asking kindly. Best, Nell Ashdown, The Ammet Courier

units.title: first proper day
units.author: sam
units.text: hi, Mum's first proper day at home. She walked to the kitchen and back four times and then announced she was 'retiring from walking'. The physio rang to check and Mum told her the dog was helping, which is a lie. The play opens tomorrow. They've moved it to the afternoon because of the power cuts, so nobody has to walk home in the dark. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: the kid asked me tonight if the trees on your island will grow back. I said yes, eventually, and she said 'good, because the birds will want them'. I didn't know what to say to that. anyway. it's freezing again. the lamp from the hall is still in my window. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: the power's gone off here again. I'm typing on my phone in the dark and the dog is pressed against my leg like a hot water bottle. It's very quiet. I can hear the church clock, which I never can. I know you can't write back. I just like knowing it's going to your inbox. S x

units.title: mum says
units.author: sam
units.text: Mum says to tell you to wear a hat. She says it every time I mention you, it's become a sort of chorus. 'Wear a hat.' So, from Mum: wear a hat. From me: sleep, eat something hot, and don't do anything silly with a chainsaw in the dark. S x

units.title: Window lamp (Gilliver custom): current practice
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Current practice. The custom declined through the later twentieth century and by the 1990s was kept by perhaps a dozen Gilliver households, mostly older residents. It is once again widely observed in Gilliver this month, coinciding with a period of night-time power cuts in the Sound; battery lamps are now common. [citation needed: no formal count has been made; editor's own observation and local reports]

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. The addition above is journalism, not history, and an encyclopaedia has no business recording what happened last week. That said, I accept the society should note revivals when they occur, and the editor has marked it honestly. I suggest we revisit it in a year and see whether the lamps are still lit when the power is back. Pell.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Reply. Agreed, with one amendment: the note records an observation, not an interpretation. I have deliberately not said why households have taken it up again. Some say it is the power cuts, some the camp lights on the Holm, and some say only that their mothers did it. The article will not choose between them, as it has never chosen before.

units.title: Carrow Point log, December 1906 (excerpts, cont.)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 8th. 00:00 wind SW 2, vis 10 miles, barometer 30.30 falling. Lamp burning well. 02:00 haze over the Holm. Remarks: none on the road. Assistant reports that he did not sleep in his off-watch, there being a sound on the roof of the dwelling at intervals, which I attribute to the frost loosening the slates. I have told him to stop his ears with wool.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 11th. 00:00 calm, vis excellent, barometer 30.38. Lamp burning well. Gilliver dark save the harbour window. Remarks: Four on the shore road at 01:50, more than heretofore. Standing, facing the light. Assistant would not come to the gallery. I did not insist. Entered here only. The Board's instructions are silent and so shall I be.

units.title: Penhallow camp diary: January 1895, continued
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Jan 19th. Calm. 12 trees. Doble and Pascoe would not go past the second stack, said they could not see the yard lamp from there. Mr Ashby let them stop. The long hut lamp burned all night and both lamps in the cook house too. Oil short. I have written for more by the boat and underlined it.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Jan 20th. Sabbath. No work. No lesson read. Mr Ashby kept to his bunk. Eight men and the cook, Lusk having gone across on the morning boat without his tools. Frost so hard the ink is thick. I keep the lamp book. Lamps all night, all huts.

units.title: Miss Arnell's notebook: Kittering Holm survey (cont.)
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Ninth day. Marked sticks at the north landing untouched again. Checked the shore for otter spraint: none, though the Gilliver side has plenty. A day of absences. [sketch: empty shoreline, a tide line of wrack] Pengelly says his grandfather took a dog across once and it would not get out of the boat. I asked when. He said before my time, miss, and rowed faster.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 23, side B
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Your brother says he got to a hundred on the slip. / Mrs M. Rowe (b. 1912): He never. He got to sixty and came up the slip like a cat. I was on the wall. / Interviewer: Was there anyone else there? / Mrs R.: Only us kids. [pause] And the fellow at the end, but he was always there in those days. We thought he was a fisherman. Nobody minded him.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Which fellow? / Mrs R.: At the end of the slip. Standing. You'd see him in the fog. My mother said it was old Tremayne waiting for his boat. / Interviewer: Tremayne of the curing station? / Mrs R.: I suppose. [laughs] I don't know, love, I was eight. Put down that it was Tremayne. [Interviewer's note: Mr Tremayne died in 1911, before the subject's earliest memories.]

units.title: Talbot survey (1953): appendix A, party diary (cont.)
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: Day 5. Levelling completed to the south point. The hollow at the south point is wet and was not surveyed in detail. Boat at 15:20. Day 6. Rain. Party remained at Gilliver. Day 7. Chainman Pengelly (the boatman's nephew) declined to land. Replaced by Coombe's brother at the same rate. Work proceeded. Boat at 15:30. All present.

units.title: LB-0377: Carrow Point, last foghorn soundings
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0377. Date: November 1999. Location: Carrow Point headland, 200 m from the light. Kit: DAT, stereo pair. Duration: 38:20. Content: the old diaphone foghorn in its final month before replacement, sounding every 30 s, with compressor noise between blasts. Recordist's note: 'You hear the compressor ticking over all night if it's still.' Curator's note: the replacement emitter is electronic and has no compressor.

units.title: From the archive: 'Gilliver Notes', November 1897
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The young men of the village have revived, we hear, the foolish wager of standing at the slip end after nightfall with their backs to the water, the prize being a quart of ale at the Anchor. Your correspondent has no objection to ale but much to drowning, and begs the fathers of Gilliver to put a stop to it before the winter fogs.

units.title: Amos Rendle's diary, 1936 (excerpts, cont.)
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 6. Calm again, a third night. Will would not come. Sat up by the window lamp with his boots on as if to go and never went. Mother said leave him. I went with Uncle Joe and we did not go past the Skerry. Joe said he would not either in this calm, you can hear too far. 4 boxes. Price poor.
